# Deciding in a review

A goal behind leaves a review with a next step (an owner and a week) or an accepted risk with a reason; the next session opens with what the last one agreed.

## The rule

**Who may speak for a review** (`canSpeakFor`): someone in it, or an admin. Marking a goal reviewed, a note, the review accepting a risk, and a question or next step raised in the review are refused for anyone else with "Only people in {review}, or an admin, can speak for it." (`speakRefusal`). Even then, only about a goal the review walks (its goals, trees and levels, `goalsIn`): anything said in it about another goal is refused with "{review} doesn’t cover {goal}, so nothing can be said about it there." (`scopeRefusal`). Everyone may read a review, and anyone may still ask a question or agree a next step on a goal's own page. A review's page tells someone not in it who can add them (`joinLine`): "You’re not in this review. {its people and whoever set it up, up to six, then "and {n} more"} or an admin can add you."

**Who must decide.** A goal whose status is `off` or `risk` (`needsDecision`) is not marked reviewed in a walk until something is decided about it. Every other goal is marked reviewed as before.

**What counts as a decision** (`decisionFor`), the latest in the session first:
- a **next step** said in this session: an action with a person who does it and a week it is due by (open or done). An action without a week, a note or a question is not a decision;
- the review **accepting the risk**: a note said in the session whose words are "We accept the risk: " and then the reason, at least 5 characters (`acceptRisk`; `acceptedReason` reads it back). It is a look, not a plan: the goal still needs attention;
- or, wherever it was agreed (the goal's page, say), an open action on the goal with a person and a week, agreed since the goal's latest check-in and not yet overdue. This is the record [needs attention](flags.md) reads for "being handled".

**Choosing who does it** is find-and-pick ([finding things](finding.md)): you and your team are suggested before anything is typed; then the people whose name, job title or team has a word starting with each word typed, those whose name it starts first, never someone marked as left. It is the one person search, the same as People's.

**Last time** (`lastTime`): the session before this one is the latest earlier week anything was said in the review. Its actions are listed with how each stands now: open, overdue (open past its week) or done; open ones first, then by due week.

**Finishing** marks every goal not yet reviewed, in one save with Undo (`markReviewed`; Undo is `unmarkReviewed`), and so holds the session. Before it does, it says what was decided (`sessionDecisions`): the next steps by who owns them, the risks accepted, and the questions still open.

**To do** (`sessionToDo`): a person's session counts as something to do (the Reviews count, Home's main action) when it is this week's, not held, and either its day has come or a goal in it has been checked in on. So a workspace set up this morning doesn't say a review is to do.

## Limits the records hold

Faro’s database holds these as well as the rule; a rebuild holds them wherever it stores the records. The constraint names are in `spec/core/schema.sql`, which is for reading, not copying.

- A decision’s due week, when it has one, is 0 to 53. (`okr_decisions_due_week_check`)
- A review is held every 1 to 13 weeks. (Its set-up screen offers 1, 2 or 4; the rule allows any of 1 to 13.) (`okr_reviews_every_weeks_check`; the code holds it too, in `src/domain/actions.ts`)
- A review’s day is a day of the week, 0 to 6. (The app’s rule asks for Monday to Friday, 0 to 4.) (`okr_reviews_weekday_check`; the code holds it too, in `src/domain/actions.ts`)
- A review has a name. (`okr_reviews_name_check`)

## Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| Which statuses need a decision: off, risk, on, stale, done. | `yes, yes, no, no, no` |
| The words saved for accepting the risk because "the vendor fix lands next release", and what is read back from them and from "Talked it through". | `We accept the risk: the vendor fix lands next release / the vendor fix lands next release / not a decision` |
| In the demo workspace, Daniel accepts the risk on the merge queue in the Developer Productivity fortnightly with the reason "ok". | `refused: Say why the review accepts the risk.` |
| In the demo workspace, Daniel, who is in the Developer Productivity fortnightly, marks a goal the fortnightly doesn’t walk reviewed in it. | `refused: Developer Productivity fortnightly doesn’t cover {that goal}, so nothing can be said about it there.` |
| In the demo workspace, Oskar, who is not in the Developer Productivity fortnightly and is not an admin, marks the merge queue reviewed in it. | `refused: Only people in Developer Productivity fortnightly, or an admin, can speak for it.` |
| Searching the demo workspace’s people for "kap", then "rhea tunde". | `Rhea Kapoor / nobody` |

## Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** Accepting the risk is stored as a note whose words start with a fixed phrase, so no new kind of record was needed before the talk. A rebuild should give it a kind of its own (a decision with a reason), and keep the phrase only for what people read.

## Requirements

- `REVIEW-DECIDE`: A goal off track or at risk leaves a review's walk with a decision: a next step with an owner (chosen by searching, never from a list of everyone) and a week it's due by, or "We accept the risk" with a reason. The goal page shows next steps as dated rows with an owner, changed there, an overdue one flagged; anyone can add one. The next session opens with what the last one agreed and asks if it's done. Finish review says what was decided and who owns what, with Undo. A review isn't "to do" before anything is due.
- `REVIEW-RUN`: What was said in a review is kept as its summary; owners see questions and actions on their goal page.
- `REVIEW-SPEAK`: Only someone in a review, or an admin, speaks for it: marking a goal reviewed, a note, accepting a risk, and a question or next step raised in it are refused for anyone else with one sentence, through the app and the AI tools alike. Everyone can still read it. Its page tells someone not in it who can add them, and never offers a Join it refuses.
